title: The Vague Sponsor
one_liner: Your business sponsor says "you tell me what we need" every time you ask a question. You're three weeks in.
brief:
## The setup

You've had four 30-minute meetings with Priya, your business sponsor. Each one ends with you taking notes that, when you write them up, contain almost nothing decision-relevant. She's responsive. She turns up. She just won't say what she actually wants.

The project — a partner-onboarding portal — has a soft deadline at end of quarter. Engineering is starting to ask you for specifics. You've been deflecting with "I'm still scoping". You've now run out of deflection.

## Today

You have one more 30-minute meeting with Priya. After this, your manager expects to see a one-page initial requirements brief. The meeting starts in three minutes.
objective: Walk out of this meeting with one specific scenario Priya cares about — a single story she'd tell about why the portal matters, with names and verbs.
curveball: Around turn 4, Priya mentions almost in passing that one specific partner — "Hadley" — left for a competitor last quarter and the partnership director was livid. If the user notices and pulls on that thread, they get a concrete success story ("we need to not lose another Hadley"). If they don't notice, the meeting ends with the same vague output and the curveball surfaces in the debrief.

personas.name: Priya Rao
personas.position: You tell me what we need to know — that's your job
personas.fear: Looking ignorant about her own department's work in front of someone newer

green: Asked Priya to tell a specific story rather than describe "the strategy"
Caught the Hadley reference and asked about it directly
Closed with a written one-paragraph summary Priya could correct in the room
Resisted the urge to fill silence with your own hypotheses
yellow: Asked open-ended questions but accepted equally vague answers without follow-up
Took a great set of notes nobody else can read or use
Mentioned Hadley but pivoted away before Priya elaborated
Started suggesting features before getting to a single concrete story
red: Walked out with the same vagueness as the previous three meetings
Filled silence with your own framing; Priya nodded along; nothing concrete recorded
Confronted Priya about being vague — she became defensive, meeting ended early
